grammar.structure: Would you like…? / What would you like?
grammar.example: What would you like to drink?
Could we have the check, please?
Would you like some more bread?
A salad without onions, with the dressing on the side.

tips.en: In the US you ask for "the check" (la cuenta). The waiter usually won't bring it until you ask, or brings it when you finish.
tips.es: En Estados Unidos se pide «the check» (la cuenta). El mesero normalmente no la trae hasta que la pides, o la trae al terminar.

tips.en: Tipping 15–20% is expected in restaurants with table service.
tips.es: En restaurantes con servicio a la mesa se espera una propina del 15 al 20%.

tips.en: Water is free: "Can I have a glass of water, please?" Refills of soft drinks are often free too.
tips.es: El agua es gratis: «Can I have a glass of water, please?». Rellenar el refresco también suele ser gratis.

tips.en: Portions are big. Ask for "a to-go box" to take the rest home.
tips.es: Las porciones son grandes. Pide «a to-go box» para llevarte lo que sobre.

tips.en: If you have an allergy, say: "I'm allergic to…" — restaurants take it seriously.
tips.es: Si tienes una alergia, di: «I'm allergic to…»: los restaurantes lo toman en serio.

phrases.es: Una mesa para dos, por favor.

explanation.en: "I'll have…" is the natural way to order.
explanation.es: «I'll have…» es la forma natural de pedir.

question.en: You finished eating and want to pay. You say:
question.es: Terminaste de comer y quieres pagar. Dices:

options: Could we have the check, please?
Could we have the bill to go?

question.en: In a US restaurant with table service, the usual tip is…
question.es: En un restaurante de Estados Unidos con servicio a la mesa, la propina habitual es…

question.en: You can't eat nuts. You say:
The sweet course at the end of a meal is…
question.es: El plato dulce al final de la comida es…

explanation.en: In offers we use "some", even in questions.
explanation.es: En ofrecimientos se usa «some», aunque sea pregunta.

question.en: You can't finish your food and want to take it home. You ask for…
question.es: No terminas tu comida y quieres llevártela. Pides…

explanation.en: A to-go box = recipiente para llevar.
explanation.es: A to-go box = recipiente para llevar.

question.en: The waiter asks "Are you ready to order?" but you need more time. You say:
question.es: El mesero pregunta «Are you ready to order?» pero necesitas más tiempo. Dices:

options: Not yet. Could we have a few more minutes?

explanation.en: "Not yet" + polite request for more time.

story.title: A New York Diner
story.text: On her last night in New York, Carmen invites Elena to dinner at an old diner. "A table for two, please," says Carmen. The waitress gives them the menus. "What would you like to drink?" "Two coffees, please." Carmen reads the menu slowly. "Is the chili spicy?" "A little," says the waitress. "Okay. I'll have the chili and a salad without onions." Elena orders a turkey sandwich. The portions are enormous! "Would you like some dessert?" asks the waitress. "Apple pie, please. Two forks." At the end, Carmen asks, "Could we have the check, please? And can I get a to-go box?" She calculates the tip: twenty percent. Elena watches her and smiles. "You order like a New Yorker now." "Thirty lessons ago I didn't know how to say 'tenedor'!"
story.es: En su última noche en Nueva York, Carmen invita a Elena a cenar a un diner antiguo. «Una mesa para dos, por favor», dice Carmen. La mesera les da los menús. «¿Qué les gustaría tomar?» «Dos cafés, por favor.» Carmen lee el menú despacio. «¿El chili pica?» «Un poco», dice la mesera. «Bueno. Para mí el chili y una ensalada sin cebolla.» Elena pide un sándwich de pavo. ¡Las porciones son enormes! «¿Les gustaría postre?», pregunta la mesera. «Pay de manzana, por favor. Dos tenedores.» Al final, Carmen pregunta: «¿Nos trae la cuenta, por favor? ¿Y me da un recipiente para llevar?» Calcula la propina: veinte por ciento. Elena la mira y sonríe. «Ahora pides como una neoyorquina.» «¡Hace treinta lecciones no sabía decir «fork»!»
